title: TRACE: Topology-Aware Reconnection via Prediction-Adaptive Connectivity Enforcement for Thin-Structure Segmentation
abstract: arXiv:2610.22210v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Thin, elongated structures are particularly sensitive to connectivity errors, as even a few local segmentation mistakes can disrupt otherwise continuous paths. Existing skeleton-based objectives typically supervise fixed centerline locations and do not account for alternative local routes that may restore connectivity. We propose TRACE, a topology-aware, prediction-adaptive objective that uses a target skeleton to define required local connections. For each connection, TRACE identifies the easiest valid reconnection under the current prediction and jointly supervises its bottleneck with the corresponding skeleton point. The supervision thus adapts to the evolving prediction rather than remaining fixed to the centerline. We further introduce a topology-aware skeleton carrier that preserves both foreground and class-specific topology, enabling reliable definition of these connections. Extensive experiments across six 2D and 3D benchmarks

translated_title: TRACE：面向细长结构分割的拓扑感知重连方法——通过预测自适应的连接性强化
translated_abstract: 细长结构对连通性错误特别敏感，因为即使少量的局部分割错误也可能破坏原本连续的路径。现有的基于骨架的目标函数通常监督固定的中心线位置，而未考虑可能恢复连通性的替代局部路径。我们提出了TRACE，这是一种拓扑感知、预测自适应的目标函数，它利用目标骨架来定义所需的局部连接。对于每个连接，TRACE在当前预测下识别最容易实现的有效重连路径，并将其瓶颈与相应的骨架点进行联合监督。因此，这种监督方式能够随着预测的演进而自适应调整，而非固定于中心线。我们进一步引入了一种拓扑感知的骨架载体，能够同时保留前景和类别特定的拓扑信息，从而可靠地定义这些连接。在六个2D和3D基准数据集上进行了大量实验。
tldr: 提出TRACE方法，一种拓扑感知且预测自适应的分割目标函数，通过在当前预测下识别最容易的有效重连路径，并将其瓶颈与骨架点联合监督，从而有效提升细长结构分割的拓扑连通性。
en_tdlr: TRACE is a topology-aware, prediction-adaptive objective for thin-structure segmentation that identifies the easiest valid reconnection under the current prediction and jointly supervises its bottleneck with skeleton points to enforce connectivity.
